Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  August 3, 2023

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on August 3, 2023. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:09 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Vacant - District 2,
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3, Commissioner Henry
  Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:  Commissioner Christopher Beck- District 4

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Sabrina Barnes  Director
  Craig Civitello  Park Maintenance Lead Worker
  Bharat Devlia  Food Services Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Mary Rosounet-Rouzan  Recreation Supervisor

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner
McLemore that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on,
August 3, 2023 be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Denmon, McLemore
Noes: None

STAFF REPORTS. A staff report recommending the Park and Recreation Commission
discuss and recommend the Park Projects Priority List for approval by the Mayor and
Council Members was presented for consideration.

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner McLemore that the
Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:
Ayes: Brown, Fragoso, Denmon, McLemore, and Beck
Noes: None

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. The Park Maintenance Supervisor Juan Mata,
reported that for the month of July, staff replaced two slides at park playgrounds - one at
Siminski and one at Rogers Park. Staff also placed a new planter in front of the Main Library
and installed all new landscaping at the Crenshaw-Imperial Branch Library. Staff replaced
four trees at Vincent Park that had been broken due to vandalism, replaced three toilets
and two sinks at Rogers Park restroom, and repaired three irrigation main brakes at
Vincent Park. Gilbert Gonzalez, Graffiti Abatement Supervisor, reported District 1,
especially Vincent Park was heavily targeted - throughout the park restrooms and tennis
area, as well as District 2’s North Park area and the park itself. Staff provided the graffiti
hotline number - (310) 412-8739.

REPORTS - RECREATION. The Recreation Superintendent, Teresa Estrada, reported the
following: MOVIES IN THE PARK – The Summer “Movies in the Park” series has been a
huge success with over 400 residents and families coming out thus far to enjoy an
unforgettable evening of cinema under the stars. Join us on Saturday, August 12 for the
final movie of the series. The Super Mario Bros Movie will be shown on the big screen at
North Park. The movie will begin at dusk. There will be free popcorn and food and
refreshments will be available for purchase. SWIMMING POOL - The Edward Vincent Park
Swim Complex has served over 500 youth and adults this summer. They offer youth and
adult swim lessons, Parent & Me Swim Classes, Lap Swim, and Aqua Fitness classes for
Seniors. If you are looking to beat the heat, general swim is offered Tuesday through
Saturday from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. The swim complex also offers themed Family Swim
Nights each week (go over flyer). The swimming pool will close on Saturday, September 2.
SUMMER CAMP RECAP - This year, the Parks, Recreation and Community Services
Department provided a fun-filled summer to over 800 campers ages 3-12. Campers
enjoyed a different theme each session, as well as participated in, enrichment
programming, specialty activities, field trips, and more! Camp will culminate on Friday,
August 11. HISPANIC HERITAGE FESTIVAL - This year’s annual Hispanic Heritage Festival
will take place on Saturday, September 23 from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. in downtown Inglewood
on Market Street. There will be live entertainment, classic car show, information and
vendor booths, health screenings, arts and crafts, face painting and a food court cooking
up delicious and authentic food. The festival is FREE and open to the public. Don’t forget
to mark your calendars and save the date for this exciting event.

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. SUMMER FOOD/ CACFP PROGRAM: The Food Service
Manager Bharat Devlia reported on the following: The Summer Food Program started on
June 12, 2023. The program hours are Monday through Friday, providing breakfast, lunch
and snacks at seven sites (Sites and Serving Time listed below). An average of 350 meals
are served per week.

The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) serves meals to youth 18 years old and
under and operates at four sites (Crenshaw Library, Inglewood Main Library, Rogers Park,
and Darby Park). The anticipated start date for CACFP is October 2, 2023.

SENIOR CENTER OPERATIONS: The senior center has been quite active over the past two
months with attendance approaching the following pre-COVID numbers. The following
events took place within that time frame:
   June 14 – Transportation Day Event
   June 16 – Father’s Day Celebration with special performances
   June 30 – Art Sculpture Installation (now on display)
   July 1 – Metro changes fare structure
   June/July – Voting in of new ISCAC Members

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

    July 13 – Office of Emergency Services, conducted an Earthquake Safety class
    July 18/25 and Aug 1/8/15 Metro’s on the Move Program Workshops
    August 17 – OES to conduct Emergency Preparedness Safety class

The senior center recently introduced two new activities (Puzzles Time and Adult Coloring),
which seniors are enjoying. Previously completed puzzles are now on display in the Fir
room for senior’s viewing pleasure. Staff also hosted a Paint and Sip class that seniors
enjoyed.

SENIOR/DISABLE TRANSPORTATION: The paratransit program continues to provide more
trips to seniors/disabled who are enrolled in the Transportation Program. Additionally,
the new taxi program has been transitioning away from the voucher program to get ready
to distribute the new taxi cards that seniors/disabled will start using. A 3-month transition
period is being allowed to provide an opportunity for seniors to use their remaining taxi
voucher coupons. With this change in the taxi card system, staff expects to improve the
overall taxi service experience.

Metro recently had a fare structure change (July 1, 2023). Their fare structure for the
general public, seniors, and the disabled community was affected. Seniors will no longer
be able to purchase monthly passes as they once did and in place of that, senior/disabled
persons can now purchase $20 worth of fare value for $10. Metro has daily peak
($0.75/ride) and off-peak ($0.35/ride) rates. If a senior/disabled patron rides in a day and
reaches $2.50, after reaching that cap, the remaining day would be free. If a senior spends
$5.00, they will receive a week of free fare once the $5 cap is reached. This new fare
structure is a pay as you go type program, which can be beneficial to those who utilize
public transportation.

The I-Line Trolley will have a stop at the new Target located at 220 N. LaBrea/Florence
added to its route. It’s anticipated the new stop will be active in the next few weeks.
Paratransit drivers met with IPD Sgt. LaGreek as well as the City’s Risk Manager to talk
about accidents and highlight critical points related to traffic safety.

SENIOR NUTRITION: Approximately 400 seniors are served per week through home-
delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate lunches at our Senior Center.
Additionally, the Center continues to provide fresh produce to seniors weekly in
collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute. We are pleased to share that our
Nutrition programs are now exceeding the pre-COVID levels of service. On Friday, August
11, we will be serving a special Hawaiian Luau menu, including Braised Hawaiian Chicken,
Green Beans, Brown Rice Pilaf, Spinach Salad with Mandarin Oranges, Seasonal Fresh Fruit,
Hawaiian Sweet Bread, and Pineapple Upside Down Cake. Our Hawaiian celebration will

include fun activities and we encourage all to dress in their favorite Hawaiian shirts and
clothing.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. Sabrina Barnes reported on the following Capital Improvement
updates: 1) Pump Track completed at Vincent Park. 2) Restroom II Phase 2 is under
construction at Vincent Park as well as Restroom 1 Phase 1 at Darby Park. 3) The walking
track at Darby Park goes before City Council next month. 4) Budget Prep: there are four
projects recommended for general fund funding; Phase III of the Restroom Improvement
Project at Vincent Park; the Swimming Pool Deck Improvement at Vincent Park; and, the
Darby Park Lighting Improvement Project. Use of Measure A grant funds recommended
for Rogers Park Ballfields, North Park improvements, Queen Park Improvement Project,
and Ashwood Park Fountain (converted to a Planter).

PUBLIC COMMENTS. Angela Evans stated the Darby Park Pickleball community would like
a cover on top of the fence for protection from the sun and additional parking.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Brown made comments regarding graffiti at
Vincent Park, the Martin Luther King Celebration, and American Legion Baseball.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:58 p.m.
